pages.text: A brain is only a clock that has stopped. Set one on a $(l)Dissection Table$() and it waits in its jar for what it is missing: $(l)Awareness$() to think with, and $(l)Time$() to think in.$(br2)Sixteen drams of each.

pages.title: Feeding the Brain
pages.text: Awareness cannot be carried in glass, so point the $(l)Tap$() of an Awareness organism at the table and let it pour. Time can come the same way, or from a $(l)Stasis Ampoule$() by hand.$(br2)Use the table with an empty hand to see how far along it is. Sneak to lift the brain out again.

pages.title: The Spark
pages.text: Put $(l)lightning rods$() on the table's frame: on top of it, or around it. Then wait for a storm, or call the lightning down yourself with a $(l)Channeling$() trident.$(br2)If the brain is ready, it wakes. If it is not, it cooks. Brains are not easy to come by.
